verdict.rationale: Adyen is API-first: server-to-server Checkout API calls, API-key auth, a separate test environment with test credentials, and idempotent retries all support unattended automation. Its MCP server also runs non-interactively via npx, with the API key passed through an environment variable. However, nothing in the evidence documents CI usage itself, such as a CLI, pipeline integration, or headless test-run guidance, so coverage of the story is only partial. missing for 10: an official CLI or documented CI/pipeline workflow, explicit headless or automated test-run guidance, and independent hands-on corroboration of CI automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Your server makes three Checkout API requests: /paymentMethods, /payments, and /payments/details.
the API key is passed via the ADYEN_API_KEY environment variable
Test the different types of transactions with Adyen that your integration handles using test credentials.
The Adyen API supports idempotency, allowing you to retry a request multiple times while only performing the action once.
